collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — HISTORY AND COLLECTIVE MEMORY (HIS-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Old stories, ruins and abandoned places, heirlooms, disputed records, festivals that changed, names on carvings, customs nobody can explain, and the things a people remembers together: some of it painful and handled gently, some of it gloriously silly.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an elder fisher or an elder and a young adult, 18-25)

collection.description: An elder brings a young villager to hang their first fishhook on the old wall of hooks: hang it with a story, or quietly.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: In the canoe house, there's a wall of old fishhooks hung on pegs: bone, shell, stone, wood, and a few made of metal, some so old they're nearly crumbling. Every fisher who ever worked from this beach hung their first hook there. Today (friend) has made (friend.his/her) own first hook, and (subject) has brought (friend.him/her) to the wall.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) tells (friend.him/her) how it's done: you hang your hook and say one true thing about your first catch. (friend) hangs (friend.his/her) own and says, a bit embarrassed, that (friend.his/her) first fish was very small and fell back in the water. (subject) laughs and says (subject.his/her) own was a sandal. They're both on the wall now. (friend) feels taller all day.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) hangs (friend.his/her) hook without a word, next to all the others, and steps back. (subject) watches (friend.him/her) look at the wall, at all those hooks, generations of them. (friend) notices one hook that's almost exactly like (friend.his/her) own, very old, made by someone nobody remembers. (friend.He/she) moves (friend.his/her) own a little closer to it. (subject) doesn't say anything. (subject.He/she) doesn't need to.
